pages.text: These glyphs are involved in manipulating boolean species, species that represent either true or false. Numerically, true and false can be expressed as 1 or 0. These species are important as they are used to gate functionality by condition; for further details see the section on $(l:lingua_mundi:computation_specifics/quotations)Quotations$().

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.to_boolean
pages.text: $(n)any$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Converts a species into the corresponding boolean. If fed a boolean, returns the boolean. Returns false if fed null, a number with value 0, or an empty list. For everything else, the glyph returns true.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.bool_to_num
pages.text: $(n)boolean$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Returns either 0 or 1 depending on the value of the boolean at the head of the capsum.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.not
pages.text: $(n)boolean$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Takes a boolean and returns the opposite value.$(br)eg. False → True, or True → False

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.and
pages.text: $(n)bool, bool$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Pops two booleans, returns true only if both of the inputs have value true.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.or
pages.text: $(n)bool, bool$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Pops two booleans, returns true if at least one of the inputs has value true.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.xor
pages.text: $(n)bool, bool$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Pops two booleans, returns true only if exactly one input is true, while the other is false.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.equal
pages.text: $(n)A, B$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Pops two species, returns true if they are equal, otherwise returns false.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.compare_eq
pages.text: $(n)num, num$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Returns true if the number below the head is smaller than or equal to the number at the head.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.compare
pages.text: $(n)num, num$() → $(n)bool$()$(br)Returns true if the number below the head is strictly smaller than the number at the head.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.in_block
pages.text: $(n)vector$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Checks the vector position fed into the glyph. Returns true if the corresponding position is inside a block (solid), otherwise returns false.
